acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Skeletons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bone Knight, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Ossuary-Levy Interceptor (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Thickened reinforced bone, a plated ribcage that can open along one seam, a corroded knightly weapon, and a helm fused permanently to the skull around bright socket flame.

Signature mechanic: Bone Levy: the fused helm marks one loose bone pile with a socket-fire line, and the plated ribcage opens to receive it. Arm bones produce a long intercepting lance, ribs produce a forward cage barrier, and skulls produce a second lookout mounted on the shoulder. Only one levy can be active; striking the moving pile or the bright rib seam before it locks denies the construction and leaves the chest open.
battlefieldDuty: Change the encounter economy by claiming scattered bones from either side of the battlefield, forging them into one temporary intercepting limb, lance, or plated-rib barrier.
constructionDimensions: Materials remain funerary and necromantic rather than elemental: dry ivory bone, rusted mail, black iron, grave-cloth, jewelry, crowns, carved runes, and the source-explained socket-fire binding retain age and provenance.

Motion and effects stay bounded to articulation: jaw chatter, mail tension, bone scrape, falling grave dust, brief rune conduction between touching bones, and orbiting fragments tied to visible staff or socket anchors.
counterplay: Move or destroy the marked pile, cross the light line before the fragments reach the chest, or strike the bright rib seam during intake; once built, attack from the side the chosen bone structure cannot cover. Affinity signal: Skull sockets, mail ties, shield straps, rib seams, loose bone piles, grave seals, staff sockets, and gaps in the orbiting halo remain the established mechanic weak points.
forbiddenTreatments: Flesh, solid spectral fill, or effects that erase skeletal negative space
identityInvariants: Human or humanoid skeletal proportions remain narrow, angular, and defined by empty negative space where flesh and organs would be.
Bone white or yellowed ivory is paired with rust, black iron, tattered grave-cloth, and one explained necromantic socket-fire accent such as green, blue, or gold.
Bone, rusted mail, corroded steel, grave-cloth, funerary jewelry, and crowns remain recognizable mortuary materials rather than living anatomy.
Carved skull runes, bone spurs, fused armor-like mass, grave regalia, and orbiting fragments accumulate as binding power becomes denser.
Bone density and the intensity and reach of the visible necromantic binding escalate together, but every form preserves gaps, joints, or binding anchors that can be deliberately broken.
telegraph: The bright socket flame narrows toward one bone pile, the helm turns without the shoulders, and the plated ribcage spreads along a clearly lit central seam.
